free_tier.stated: no free plan: Cloud virtual machines start 'From €8.93/month' with free egress traffic
free_tier.notes: No trial applies to Cloud virtual machines (third-party index); a balance of at least EUR 4 is needed to start.

egress.terms: Outgoing traffic is free on virtual machines and no byte allowance is published; the cheapest shared plan lists unmetered transfer limited by port speed (200 Mbps) and fair use on a third-party index; inbound UDP is allowed by adding a custom security-group rule

interface_detail: SSH to the VPS public IPv4 address
tooling: wg-quick or any VPN daemon inside the guest
chaining: a low-priced origin with free outgoing traffic in 30+ regions; the wall is the account balance and the port speed, not a byte count

limits.value: 200 Mbps port on the Basic G2S 1 vCPU plan, with unmetered transfer 'limited by port speed and fair use' (third-party index)

binding_note: at 1 TiB a month no byte quota is published because outgoing traffic is free; the 200 Mbps port on the shared plan would carry about 65 TB a month, so neither fails first; a balance of at least EUR 4 is the entry floor

identity_cost.detail: the Gcore docs say a self-service account pays with a card or wallet, adding a card triggers a verification hold of about 1 EUR or 1 USD, and at least EUR 4 must be on the balance; the services agreement lets Gcore require KYC documents (not stated to apply to every self-service sign-up); the sign-up page is a login application and was not read

reliability_note: unverified: services are suspended when payment fails from both the balance and the payment method; no throttle behaviour is stated on the pages read
confidence_note: free outgoing traffic, the entry price and the firewall behaviour are quoted from the vendor's own pages read on 2026-11-04; the Basic shared plan's port and price rest on a third-party index and are reported; no VM was ordered and no port was probed

evidence.quote: Dedicated vCPUs, including free egress traffic and billing only for active instances.
evidence.proved: the Standard VM line states free egress traffic and billing only for active instances
the vendor's own entry price for a VM is EUR 8.93 a month

evidence.quote: The Windows license is charged separately. Outgoing traffic is free.

evidence.quote: To start using Edge Cloud services, add at least €4 or

evidence.proved: adding a card triggers a verification hold of about EUR 1

evidence.quote: The default security group allows inbound traffic over ICMP, SSH (TCP/22), and RDP (TCP/3389 and UDP/3389).
evidence.proved: the default security group allows ICMP, SSH and RDP inbound only

evidence.quote: Template rules (All TCP/All UDP/SSH/HTTP/HTTPS/MySQL/DNS TCP/DNS UDP/PostgreSQL/RDP TCP/RDP UDP): template rules come with pre-configured protocols and ports for typical connections
evidence.proved: a custom rule or the All UDP template opens a UDP port, so a WireGuard listener can be allowed

evidence.quote: By default, all outbound traffic is allowed.
evidence.proved: outbound traffic is allowed by default

evidence.quote: The Customer is required to furnish all necessary documentation for KYC verification, and all contracts with Gcore are contingent upon successful completion of the KYC check.

evidence.quote: Gcore lists this plan at 0.71 EUR excluding VAT.
evidence.proved: the cheapest Basic G2S 1 vCPU plan is listed at EUR 0.71 a month excluding VAT, before a separate IPv4 charge

price_per_tb_month: EUR 8.93 a month for the Standard entry plan, with free outgoing traffic; no per-TB price
notes: A third-party index lists a shared Basic G2S 1 vCPU / 1 GB plan at EUR 0.71 a month excluding VAT plus EUR 2.11 for a separate IPv4 address; the vendor pages read show only the dedicated 'Standard' entry price of EUR 8.93. The existing Gcore Edge Proxy record is a different product.

extras.wg_detail: a KVM-class guest with root and a public IPv4; wg-quick binds UDP natively once a custom security-group rule opens the UDP port; inbound UDP was not probed
extras.ingress: unverified: no inbound UDP port policy is stated on the pages read
extras.volume_stated: outgoing traffic is free; no byte allowance published
extras.transit_note: bytes leave through the VM's own public address on Gcore's network
